#1895. Man United transfer news: Liverpool, Red Devils among clubs chasing Serie A 'rising talent'

By Darren Plant | 07 Nov 2026 12:09

Liverpool and Manchester United have allegedly identified AC Milan defender Koni De Winter as a potential transfer target.

The two North-West rivals are currently preparing for their final Premier League fixtures before the November international break.

Andoni Iraola's side face Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park before Michael Carrick's outfit square off against Aston Villa at Old Trafford later on Sunday.

Despite the clubs sitting at opposite ends of the Premier League table, it has become apparent that they each need to strengthen in the defensive third of the pitch.

According to Caught Offside, De Winter has emerged as a possible addition for both clubs.

The report alleges that scouts have been 'closely monitoring' the 24-year-old in recent weeks.

De Winter has made a total of 13 starts and one substitute outing in Serie A and the Europa League this season.

Although AC Milan have been inconsistent under Ruben Amorim, the Belgium international is seemingly enhancing his reputation at San Siro.

Nevertheless, it is said that De Winter is currently not actively pursuing a move away from AC Milan.

He is currently only in his second campaign at the club since leaving Genoa, while the eight-cap international has been given a more trusted role under Amorim than by his predecessor in 2025-26.

While De Winter is seemingly progressing well under Amorim, that does not necessarily mean that he is the right choice for Liverpool or Man United.

In the latter's case, they could benefit from proven Premier League quality being added to their defence, as well as someone who can eventually replace Harry Maguire.

Similar applies with Liverpool. Even if Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Giovanni Leoni are viewed as three strong centre-back options for the future, the Merseyside giants will likely target someone more experienced than De Winter to replace Virgil van Dijk.

#1893. I watched Rangers beat St Mirren and spotted penalty controversy, growing Ibrox influence and big achievement

Rangers returned to winning ways on the road with a 2-0 victory over St Mirren in Paisley on Saturday night, extending their unbeaten domestic run to 12 matches in the process.

Derek McInnes' side had been held to draws in their previous two league fixtures away from home against Dundee and Hearts, but goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil ensured there would be no repeat disappointment at the Marbill Coaches Stadium.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The result leaves the Ibrox side just one point behind Celtic at the top of the Scottish Premiership, although the league leaders have the opportunity to extend their advantage when they face Kilmarnock this afternoon.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold in Paisley for The Scotsman and picks out his three main takeaways from the game.

Rangers have now gone 12 matches without defeat in all competitions, a remarkable improvement given the uncertainty that followed McInnes' rocky start to life in Govan. Their success last night was thoroughly deserved but there remains considerable scope for improvement, particularly in the final third.

McInnes has warned that his team are not yet the finished article. There are still familiar frustrations he must continue to address. Rangers' inability to turn promising attacking situations into goals meant St Mirren remained in the contest for longer than they should have, while some questionable decision-making in the final third prevented the visitors from recording a more emphatic winning margin.

At the opposite end, though, Rangers continue to demonstrate the defensive resilience that has underpinned their domestic revival. Six clean sheets in 12 league outings represent a major achievement and provide McInnes with a solid base on which to build from. Olwethu Makhanya was fortunate to escape punishment for a couple of uncharacteristic errors on this occasion, but his defensive partner Emmanuel Fernandez produced a commanding performance to make up for it.

Rangers now have an international break to regroup before returning to Premiership action with a trip to Motherwell on November 21. McInnes will hope his players return refreshed, with the opportunity to build on their unbeaten sequence and address the attacking shortcomings that continue to prevent his side from reaching their full potential.

The game's major talking point came midway through the first-half when Rangers were awarded a penalty following a challenge by Samuel Ramos on James Penrice. The St Mirren man appeared to make minimal contact with the Rangers left-back inside the area, but referee Nick Walsh was quick in pointing to the spot.

Unsurprisingly, the decision did not go down well with the home support and Buddies boss Craig McLeish. They felt the contact from Ramos was insufficient to warrant a spot-kick, particularly given the nature of the challenge and Penrice's theatrical reaction as he went to ground. There was an expectation that VAR might intervene, but after a short review the incident, the official’s on-field decision was allowed to stand.

The award subsequently left onlookers and television pundits questioning whether there had been enough contact to justify the referee’s decision, with Chris Sutton stating in commentary “Penrice has played Nick Walsh like a piccolo.” While Rangers will argue that Penrice was impeded, St Mirren were left feeling aggrieved by a call that had a significant bearing on the contest.

The controversy provided Saints with a legitimate grievance and raised questions about the threshold for awarding penalties, particularly when VAR elects not to overturn the referee's original judgement. One that is sure to divide opinion...

Ryan Naderi has emerged as an increasingly influential figure during a period in which injuries to Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland have left Rangers short of attacking options. The forward has responded admirably, combining his physical presence and willingness to lead the line with an impressive goalscoring return. His six goals and three assists in his previous eight league appearances underline the extent of his recent contribution.

Against St Mirren, he provided further evidence of the growing importance he is assuming under McInnes by putting the disappointment of an early miss quickly behind him to break the deadlock from the penalty spot after 18 minutes. The German was coolness personified in his stuttered run-up before sending he goalkeeper the wrong way. Amid a hectic run of fixtures, his ability to deliver consistently is proving invaluable.

Beyond the numbers, it is Naderi's all-round game that appears to have particularly caught his manager’s eye. McInnes was effusive in his praise of the striker's physicality, work-rate and ability to stretch opposition defences post-match. His willingness to run the channels, attack space and bring others into play offers Rangers another dimension in the final third.

McInnes also revealed that Naderi has been practising penalties regularly in training, with that additional work translating into greater assurance when stepping up under pressure. Having inherited a squad without an established penalty specialist or set-piece take following James Tavernier’s exit, the Rangers boss will be pleased to have identified a player increasingly comfortable taking responsibility in decisive moments. Naderi's conversion was another demonstration of that growing confidence.

Naderi has certainly taken his opportunity to impress and strengthened his claim for a regular starting position. There is still room for improvement, but his relentless energy makes him an increasingly difficult player for McInnes to overlook. The question now is whether he can maintain those level when Rangers' attacking options return to full fitness. For the time being, he is making a compelling case to be one of the first names on the team sheet.

#1890. Rangers away-day concerns give way to renewed optimism as Dan Neil outlines blueprint for silverware

There was something reassuringly uncomplicated about Rangers' 2-0 victory over St Mirren. After a sequence of performances in which attacking promise had not always been matched by defensive security or an ability to put opponents away, this was a night when they got the fundamentals right and the points secured without undue drama.

In Dan Neil’s case, it served as a reminder that Rangers’ away form need not be a source of anxiety. They head into the international break in high spirits and safe in the knowledge that they are within touching distance of Premiership leaders Celtic.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Rangers' recent away performances had exposed a gap between their form at Ibrox and their consistency on the road. Goal scorer Neil acknowledged that concern, describing the win in Paisley as an important response to two disappointing results on their travels in recent weeks.

“It was a good result going into the break,” the stand-in captain admitted. “It was really important that we got that and got back to keeping clean sheets. One of the big things we spoke about before the game, other than clean sheets, is coming away from home and putting in a good performance. The last two away results and performances really haven't been us. We didn’t want it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

“Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. The better our away form is, the better chance we're going to stand [of winning the title]. Every good team just finds a way to win. Obviously we'd like to win by four or five goals every week, but unfortunately that's just not football. I do think it's an area that we can improve on, though.

“These are potential banana skin games. It's important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you've seen that. Our home form speaks for itself, but like I said, the last two away results haven't been great for us. So it was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us.”

The international break provides Rangers with an opportunity to recover ahead of a gruelling winter schedule, although Neil acknowledged that the interruption could also disrupt their rhythm.

”There's definitely pros and cons to international breaks,” he stated. “It's a chance to recharge your batteries a little bit after an intense run of games. But it also kind of halts your momentum a little bit. I think it's important that you take the positives out of the break.

“We can rest and recover ahead of the tough winter months. Hopefully all the boys come back unscathed and have good games with their international teams. I’ll be working hard at the training ground as well as having a few days off and we'll come back ready to fire again.”

There is also a shot at silverware on the horizon. Rangers have five fixtures to negotiate before their Premier Sports Cup final appearance, and Neil is conscious that momentum must be maintained.

“I'm sure we'll relay that message when all the boys are back together,” Neil added. “It's a great chance for us to build some momentum again after a break, going into that final. It's important that we take each test in isolation and not look too far ahead. When the final comes round, it comes round. We've got five really important fixtures before that in which we need to pick up as many points as we can.”

#1888. Former Rangers star lands first managerial job as SPFL club appoint Europa League finalist

East Fife have appointed former Rangers midfielder Scott Arfield as their new player-manager.

The 38-year-old replaces Dick Campbell who was sacked by the League One club last month after a run of eight matches without a victory.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Arfield has been without a club since departing Livingston in May after taking on the role of caretaker player-manager for the final three matches of the 2025-26 season.

The move to Bayview represents a first full-time step into management for the former Canada international, who also had two spells with Falkirk as well as stints with Huddersfield Town, Burnley, Charlotte FC and Bolton Wanderers.

“I am absolutely delighted to be the new manager of East Fife and I cannot wait to get started,” Arfield, who has signed a contract until May 2029, told the club website.

“I feel I am ready to go into coaching after learning a lot from excellent managers during my playing career, and I am grateful to East Fife for believing in me and for giving me this opportunity.

“My aim is now to create opportunities for others and to build a team which will excite East Fife supporters and attract the attention of the local community. It is a highly respected club which has great potential, and it is a privilege to be given the chance to lead it forward.”

Liam Anderson, chairman of East Fife, added: “We are delighted to have agreed a deal with Scott to become our new player-manager.

“This an innovative appointment and gives a clear indication of our ambitions going forward. I am sure that the arrival of Scott will be welcomed by our fans who are keen to see an exciting brand of football at Bayview.”

Arfield, who played for Rangers in the Europa League final four years ago, will take charge of the Fifers for the first time when Peterhead visit Bayview on Saturday. He also hopes to resume playing this month once he regains match fitness.

An East Fife statement added: "The board of directors is grateful to the interim management team of Jim Moffat, Pat Slattery and Brian Easton, who have guided the squad through the recent period of vacancy. Jim will continue as goalkeeping coach, Pat will assist with coaching while injury prevents him from playing, and Brian returns to on-field duties."

#1887. Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool: Andoni Iraola makes referee admission ahead of Selhurst Park visit

By Darren Plant | 07 Nov 2026 12:24

Andoni Iraola has reiterated that his Liverpool squad tend to be "too honest" during games.

Iraola made headlines last week when he suggested that he would tell his squad to "dive" when having their shirt pulled in future.

That claim was made after Alexander Isak failed to go down, or even react, to being pulled back in the Arsenal penalty area during the first half of their Premier League fixture.

Liverpool subsequently went on to suffer a 1-0 defeat to the Gunners, who now sit three points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's Premier League game at Crystal Palace, Iraola suggested that he did not like his players being praised for their 'honesty'.

As quoted by Sky Sports, the Spaniard revealed that his players received 'congratulations' from the officials.

He said: "I don’t want to talk too much about referees. I think we are quite an honest group. Sometimes too honest, and even the other day after the game, I think the referee congratulated us.

"But I don’t know if I liked it a lot or not. But he said our behaviour has been very good overall from the players, from the staff.

"I think it has to be genuine, no? You cannot fake things. When we complain it has to be genuine complaints because I think it’s a penalty, it’s a yellow card, it’s whatever.

"I feel we are willing, obviously, we are a team that wants to press, wants to be intense, but I think the balance, there is a big difference, yes."

As per Opta, only two teams in the Premier League have been awarded fewer fouls than Liverpool.

For a high-profile club that will generally have more possession than other teams in the majority of their fixtures, it is an eye-catching statistic.

#1886. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

Dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0

Possession: Chelsea 29%-71% BrightonShots: 9-6Shots on target: 4-3Corners: 2-4Touches in opposition box: 15-10

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

There has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. He should not have allowed Neto to get to that ball first.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

Since the start of the 2024/25 season, no goalkeeper in the Premier League has made more errors leading to goals than Verbruggen’s 10. Second on that list; Sanchez, who is not in the Chelsea squad today.

Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

That is an absolute gift for the home side after a huge error from Brighton. Pedro flicks on at the near post and Wieffer makes the block near his own line. Verbruggen then tries to catch the loose ball but he and Wieffer end up getting into each others’ way. The ball then falls to Lavia, who pokes home. As they did at Craven Cottage the other night, Chelsea hit the front early.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

There was a fist pump from Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee after Romeo Lavia’s goal from the corner. It looks like MacPhee will be claiming credit for that one, even though it came thanks to an error from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. Xabi Alonso also celebrated with MacPhee.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

He might be trying to sell his shares in Chelsea, but co-owner Todd Boehly is at today’s game in the Stamford Bridge stands.

Before we get going, Stamford Bridge pays tribute to Bobby Tambling and Ken Bates, who both died over the summer. Wreaths are laid in their memory with their families carrying framed pictures of the two men.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Stamford Bridge and we are moments away from kick-off in west London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Chelsea: Martinez, Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill, Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato, Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Penders, James, Acheampong, Chavarria, Caicedo, Barco, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

Brighton: Verbruggen, Wieffer, Boscagli, Dunk, Vuskovic, Gross, Gomez, De Cuyper, Kadioglu, Yalcouye, Kostoulas.Substitutes: Steele, Struijk, Hadjam, Promise, Osman, Costinha, Cozier-Duberry, O’Riley, Oriola.

As you’d expect, there were big cheers for Emi Martinez from the Chelsea fans ahead of kick-off. He responded by shaking a fist in the air and giving them a big round of applause. This is his first game since the World Cup final for Argentina.

Chelsea had gone 77 League games without fielding a player aged 30 plus before handing goalkeeper Emi Martinez a debut today. The Argentine celebrates his 34th birthday on September 2. The last played aged 30-plus to appear for the club was Thiago Silva, who was 39 at the time.

“We are delighted to have him. To have a goalkeeper of his stature, his personality, I think he will bring a lot of qualities. I am sure he can have a straight impact. We spoke, he felt ready to play, so here we go.”

On Enzo Fernandez being left out of the matchday squad:

“We assess what is best for the team and considering everything, the situation, we need a team that is focused, with everyone involved that is fully committed and engaged with the game.”

Emiliano Martínez turns 34 on September 2 and by most tangible metrics, the goalkeeper is past his peak.

But it is the intangibles that set Martínez apart and why his availability at a knock-down price from Aston Villa convinced Chelsea to seize a market opportunity.

At £7.5m, Martínez could prove to be Chelsea’s smartest piece of business of the summer and there is little doubt he will be box-office at Stamford Bridge.

“I am delighted to be at this football club,” Martinez said. “Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I am just over the moon; I cannot wait to get started.

“I want to be successful here. I am someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it is a football club that wins titles, so I think it is a good match. I am all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100 per cent every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.”

Today's Blues. 💙✊#CFC | #CHEBHA pic.twitter.com/3FSKL8LAHm

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#1885. CM: Amorim let down again in another European debacle – the players whose stock has dropped

There are several players that are at risk of slipping down Ruben Amorim’s pecking order with displays like the one against Ferencvaros.

Calciomercato.com write that three clues add up to mean that we can say with certainty that Milan are not aiming to win the Europa League despite being one of the favourites, at least on paper. The defeats against Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros were determined by two factors.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the attitude of the squad’s key players and the inadequacy of several reserves. The dominant Adrien Rabiot, for example, seems to sink when the Europa League anthem is played. The Frenchman – captain on this occasion due to Mike Maignan’s suspension – wasn’t the only culprit, but was certainly the most obvious.

The thing squad assembled last summer by Gerry Cardinale, Amorim and the management features a strong starting eleven that can compete with anyone (as was the case in the derby), but at the same time lacks alternatives.

In several cases, it’s fair to say that the players aren’t up to the task. Filippo Terracciano’s role is emblematic: already rejected by the previous management, he remained with Milan at Amorim’s request.

His season included 45 poorly played minutes against Benfica before being substituted at half-time, a straight red card as a substitute against Salzburg, and a poor performance against Ferencvaros that drew boos from the crowd.

Doubts are also growing over Ardon Jashari, who – after a few performances that were at least adequate – continues to display obvious technical and tactical limitations. The money spent on him (over €30m) is leading many to run out of patience.

The excellent performances against RB Salzburg and Udinese seemed to have reintroduced a courageous and powerful version of Davide Bartesaghi to Milan, but the most recent test saw him revert to the flaws of last season in terms of personality and concentration.

Pervis Estupinan, on the other hand, seems to have completely disappeared from the radar, having remained on the bench for the entire match against Ferencvaros. The two left-backs have a lot of work to do, and this could influence some transfer choices too.

#1884. Arsenal target Ryan Augusto tops CIES creativity ranking

By Naim Beneddra | 07 Nov 2026 13:08

An Arsenal transfer target has emerged at the top of a global ranking of the most creative young full-backs, with a new statistical study highlighting the attacking qualities of a Brazilian prospect already on the Gunners' radar.

Red Bull Bragantino right-back Ryan Augusto, 19, has been ranked first among Under-20 full-backs and wing-backs for expected assists per 90 minutes, according to research from the CIES Football Observatory.

The youngster recorded an impressive 0.32 expected assists (xA) per 90 minutes in the study, which assessed players across 52 top-flight leagues worldwide.

His achievement provides fresh evidence of his attacking potential, just weeks after Arsenal were reported to have made initial enquiries about a possible transfer.

The North London club have been monitoring Augusto's development in Brazil, although there is no indication that their interest has progressed to a formal offer.

The CIES study, published earlier this week, examined the creative output of full-backs and wing-backs aged under 20 who had played at least 450 minutes in their respective domestic leagues.

Augusto finished first with an expected assists average of 0.32 per 90 minutes, ahead of Danish-based Frederik Emmery, who recorded 0.27, and Milan Györfi, who registered 0.23.

The statistic measures the quality of goalscoring opportunities created by a player's passes, based on the likelihood of the resulting shots producing goals.

It does not represent actual assists, nor does it establish Augusto as the world's best young defender overall. However, his position at the top of the ranking underlines his effectiveness in creating opportunities from right-back.

That attacking influence is also evident in his recent performances for Bragantino.

According to figures highlighted by Brazilian outlet Trivela, Augusto has produced 28 key passes and created five big chances in 12 Brazilian Serie A appearances this season, eight of which have come as a starter.

Despite playing fewer matches than Bragantino's other senior right-backs, Agustín Sant'Anna and Andrés Hurtado, he has already surpassed both for key passes in the league.

Sant'Anna has registered 26 across 15 appearances, while Hurtado has managed 14 in 17 matches.

Augusto's numbers are particularly notable given how recently he established himself in the first-team squad.

Having joined Bragantino's academy in 2022, initially at Under-15 level, the defender has progressed rapidly through the ranks and only began receiving regular senior opportunities this year.

He registered his first professional assist in April, during a 3-2 Copa Sudamericana victory over Blooming, and later enjoyed a sequence of six consecutive starts in the Brazilian top flight.

His playing style helps explain his strong creative figures.

Augusto is comfortable advancing along the right flank, providing width and delivering passes into dangerous areas, but he can also move inside to combine with midfielders.

That ability to contribute to different phases of possession could appeal to clubs seeking technically accomplished full-backs capable of operating in more than one attacking structure.

The Brazilian has also continued his development at international level, earning another call-up to his country's Under-20 squad for November's friendlies against Peru.

Arsenal were first linked with Augusto in October, when ESPN Brazil reported that the Premier League club had established informal contact over a potential future move.

The Gunners were understood to be considering the 19-year-old as a longer-term prospect, rather than an immediate solution for Mikel Arteta's first team.

That approach would be consistent with Arsenal's willingness to identify promising Brazilian players before they become established names in European football.

Gabriel Martinelli is a prominent example, having arrived from Ituano in 2019 before developing into a regular Premier League performer.

Augusto's circumstances are different, however, particularly because of the competition he would face at right-back.

Arteta can already call upon Jurrien Timber and Ben White in that position, while Ezri Konsa and Cristhian Mosquera provide additional defensive alternatives.

A move for Augusto would therefore raise questions about his immediate pathway into the senior side, despite his impressive attacking statistics.

The Brazilian is also under contract with Bragantino until the end of 2029, giving his current employers a strong negotiating position should Arsenal decide to pursue a deal.

Other European clubs have reportedly shown interest in the defender, but no formal bid or advanced negotiations have been confirmed.

#1882. Hearts unbeaten home record obliterated as swashbuckling Falkirk earn 31-year first

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.

#1880. This is an embarrassment – Wouter Vrancken rages after Hearts humiliation

Wouter Vrancken condemned a “ridiculous” first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Jambos, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a 5-2 victory at Tynecastle.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Jambos, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

“This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,” said Vrancken. “Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

“When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

“It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

“This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,” said Vrancken.

“Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who were good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.”

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who made it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time in 31 years.

“I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,” said Bairns manager John McGlynn. “First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

“It was well documented about the Hearts injuries and, coming off the back of the game on Thursday night (in Thun), it was always going to be difficult for them.

“We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. The goals and our play were outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

“We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. At 3pm, we never expected to be 4-0 up at half-time and certainly not 5-0 up a few minutes into the second half, which was another really good goal in transition.

“Hearts had a lot at the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it. It jumps us up into third place.

“Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.”

#1878. Why Kasper Hogh would not have taken Celtic penalty as Mika Baur injury addressed

Martin O’Neill admitted he would not have let Kasper Hogh take a second half penalty that Benjamin Nygren ended up failing to score in any case as Celtic squeezed past Kilmarnock at Parkhead.

The striker’s goal drought was extended to 16 games and he’s still to open his account at home for his new club. Defender Liam Scales was the match winner after converting a cross from Camilo Dusan in the 25th minute.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hogh had earlier endured the heartbreak of seeing a goal chalked off for a foul committed earlier in the move by Mika Baur and he snatched at a chance shortly afterwards when one-on-one with Kilmarnock ‘keeper Nico Mantl.

Hogh worked hard and was named man-of-the-match but was replaced after 70 minutes. Celtic were awarded a penalty shortly afterwards and many Celtic fans lamented Hogh not still being on the pitch to take it. However, O’Neill confirmed this wouldn’t have happened even if he had been available.

Nygren duly saw Mantl make an excellent save from his effort from 12 yards to keep Kilmarnock in the game. The visitors came close to equalising right at the death when Ieuan Owen failed to connect with a cross right in front of goal.

“We all thought Kasper had got off the mark,” said O’Neill, with reference to the goal that wasn’t. “We all thought that for about 35 seconds. I think myself that maybe he would have scored the next one had the first one counted but he worked exceptionally hard for us. I was pleased the team dug it out.

“We got the penalty but had he still been on the pitch I would not have asked him to take it. He might have missed. As it turned out, we did miss.

“In front of goal, it is proving a difficult one for him,” O'Neill added. “But he has worked exceptionally hard in the game, as he did on Thursday night (v Besiktas). I think things will come, honestly. He thought he had broken the spell but his hold up play was much, much better.”

Hogh received a warm ovation when he was replaced after 70 minutes by James Forrest. “I think that’s encouraging,” said O’Neill. “If you have the crowd behind you, if you’re working hard, they will forgive some other things. Now I am not saying that will last forever….Of course strikers live and die by their goals. But he feels we all believe in him in the dressing room, that’s encouraging for him.”

O’Neill stressed he had not seen a replay of the incident involving Baur that meant Hogh’s goal after 13 minutes was ruled off after a VAR check. Referee John Beaton was called to the monitor and he very abruptly signalled he was disallowing the strike.

“I have genuinely not seen it back because the little screen we have on the touchline is too small for me,” he said. “I can only go with what the lads were saying, they thought it was touch and go.”

O’Neill also revealed that Baur, who limped off near the end, had suffered ankle damage and has been booked in for a scan. The midfielder is due to join up with the Germany Under-21s in the international break.

“He’s in the treatment room,” he said. “His ankle is really sore and we don’t know the damage. We’ll wait until tomorrow to get a scan. Gosh, I’d hope he won’t be out terribly long but I don't know at the moment. He’s been great for us considering he’s not the tallest. He’d be about ten stone maybe not even that but his work rate is incredible. His overall reading of the game is really good and he’s not frightened.”

National South side Dover will hold all the aces and be strong favourites for the tie. However, Hill manager Gary Mansell will prepare well and his team will give everything on the day.

All connections, including the hordes of travelling fans, will relish the occasion and represent Mid Sussex football with pride and determination.

As for the 2026/27 Isthmian Premier, the league is perhaps at it historical strongest with a clutch of non-league giants all slugging it out. As we have seen over the past few weeks you take your foot off the gas for a moment you get severely punished.

Hill have had hard a fought-win cruelly snatched from their grasp at Wingate and Finchley and been taught a brutal home lesson by the league leaders Enfield Town.

It’s been tough few weeks as Hill have had to travel to Cray, Erith, St Albans, Wingate and Chatham. However, Hill are taking it all in their stride currently sitting in 11th place just a tantalising three points outside the play-off zone.

On Saturday the club travelled to league powerhouses Chatham aiming to right some previous season reversals.

Chatham’s Ben Allen drove home the first goal on 40 minutes from 30 yards. Hill responded early in the second half as centre back Jack Strange headed home a good delivery from Yoan Edoukou.

The game became very frantic as both sides gave 100% effort. Hill forged three or four excellent shooting chances, but Chatham were happy to throw bodies on the line.

On 80 minutes Charlie Lambert was presented with a golden chance but his well-hit shot was saved by the keeper. With fans on the edge of their seats Hill couldn’t quite force the issue as both clubs settled for a point.

Club Captain Keiran Rowe said: "It’s a good point but also an annoying one. We restricted them to very few chances but created quite a few ourselves. We are travelling home feeling we should have won it.

"I am very proud of how the boys have reacted to the Enfield result (6-0 loss). In the last two performances we have worked hard, stuck together and it has been much better. We just need a little piece of luck and we will be away.”

Meanwhile, the Oliva family have become very much part of the Hillians culture. Coach Berty, his wife Steph and son Luca are a major part of the operation dealing with the pathway arm of the club. Hill are lucky to have them.

Over three seasons Berty has demonstrated consistent and powerful progression with the U18s bringing club success and individual improvement. Now 2026/27 has seen the introduction of the U19 academy in association with Haywards Heath College. It’s been an instant hit with players and fans alike.

Berty in tandem with Gary Mansell has been front and centre – the pair act as administrators and managers of the football side.

The team took on Maidstone Academy at the MTC and ran out 8-0 winners, their first victory of the campaign.

Oliva said: “We are very pleased with the win especially the clean sheet, it’s a good day for us.”

As to the bond with Haywards Heath College he said: “It’s going extremely well, we have the squad for training and matchdays on a Wednesday while they receive an education and facilities that are seond to none at the college.

"The lads have access to the gym and analytics. With us they have the opportunity to play competitive football away from the first team environment’ The team now face Ebbsfleet away on November 18.”

Another two unsung Hill heroes also warrant a mention here – kit managers Nat Ellis and Dan Cross. It doesn’t seem to matter how many dirty kits land at Nat’s doorstep she just gets on with it and does a great job – while Dan is on the road delivering washed kits to away dressing rooms across the south-east, and making sure every item comes back. It’s a slick operation.

Hill might be finding Isthmian wins hard to come by right now, but the club are in great shape as we head towards Christmas. Huge opportunities await.

Celtic built on their uplifting midweek victory over Besiktas but found the going hard against Neil McCann’s well-drilled team.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dane isn’t playing badly. Never mind the goal he scored after 13 minutes that was then very harshly chopped off for a foul in the build-up. Another shot midway through the second half appeared goal-bound until a heroic block from substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara deflected the ball over the bar. Events seem to be conspiring against him.

Hogh was subbed off with 20 minutes left to very warm applause. He was sitting on the bench when he heard his name surprisingly announced as the man of the match. If this was an attempt to encourage the striker, it seemed a bit cringingly overboard.

Hogh was also on the bench when Celtic were awarded a penalty after 75 minutes so couldn’t grab the ball in an effort to put everything to bed. Nygren accepted the responsibility instead and saw Nico Mantl make a brilliant diving block to keep Kilmarnock in the game.

The fans certainly appreciated Hogh’s endeavours and clearly believe that while the statistics books might state otherwise, he has already morally broken his Parkhead duck.

His neat finish was cruelly chalked off - after the Dane had completed the understandably comprehensive celebration routine - for a foul by Mika Baur in the build-up that very few saw. Referee John Beaton nevertheless seemed very sure having been called to his monitor and spent little time deliberating.

A clearly agitated Hogh then wasted a good chance to score shortly afterwards although credit should go to Mantl, the true man of the match, for blocking with his foot when the striker had just the keeper to beat. Mantl's later penalty stop - after a VAR check confirmed a handball by Aaron Tshibola had taken place inside the box – meant bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock were still fighting until the end.

They came so close to taking the point their efforts certainly deserved. With the clock having ticked into the four minutes of additional time, substitute Eric Ring reached the byline and swung in a cross that Ieuan Owen somehow failed to connect with in the middle.

As for Celtic, with their No. 9 seemingly so out of touch and luck, their No. 5 stepped in. Scales scored the kind of goal that is eluding Hogh at present after he got on the end of Duran’s floated cross. The ball kissed the crossbar before landing in the net. That’s three goals for the defender this season – equal with Hogh.

A planned period of silence to commemorate the war dead was cut short before kick-off due to the volume of booing in the stadium. Beaton barely gave it ten seconds before blowing his whistle. It all felt a little unsettling with Celtic taking longest to get themselves focused, at the risk of very nearly conceding the first goal. As was the case at the death, the visitors came close to scoring right at the start. Tom Lowery even had two bites at the cherry, with Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone the equal to his efforts both times.

Celtic sought to take advantage of the let-off and immediately got on with the seeming job in hand: helping Hogh get off the mark at Parkhead. Nygren tried to place a cross on his head after eight minutes but the striker was crowded out. It was almost as if the team had been specifically set up to let Hogh score. And he did. 4.13pm, the moment Celtic Park had been waiting for – or so it seemed.

With Jota, making his first start since April 2025, and Camilo Duran either side of Hogh and Nygren in the space behind, it ought to have been a centre-forward’s dream. Especially given all these players seemingly had one aim in mind: feed the Hogh.

Parkhead exploded with joy unconfined. Duran slipped the ball through to Nygren, who swivelled and played in Hogh. The Dane could not miss and to be fair, he didn’t. A very composed finish into the corner had him pointing to the heavens and crossing himself and making all manner of gestures of gratitude before VAR delivered the mother of all smackdowns: Goal disallowed.

Celtic secured the three points in the end, albeit with one or two scares. They have reached the latest international break in marginally better shape than last time, when successive Rangers defeats meant Martin O’Neill’s job seemed in very real jeopardy.

Charalampos Kostoulas - 6: The Greek striker had a couple of chances - one header from distance and one clever lobbed attempt - but very little fell his way. Impressive work rate. Taken of in the closing stages for Georginio.
